filename: Time series predictions in unmonitored sites_ a survey of machine learning techniques in water resources.pdf
title: Time Series Predictions in Unmonitored Sites: A Survey of Machine Learning Techniques in Water Resources
testbed_rationale: This paper is a survey and review of machine learning methodologies in water resources and does not introduce or evaluate new benchmark datasets or simulation testbeds.
pain_points: Sparse and declining observational monitoring networks (e.g., USGS monitoring reaches <1% of streams)
Spatial extrapolation to unmonitored sites (zero-shot regional transfer) is fundamentally difficult
Static representation of inherently dynamic catchment attributes (e.g., land cover, land use, water clarity)
Imbalanced datasets and poor capture of rare extreme events like floods and droughts when optimizing traditional mean squared error losses
High computational demand and equifinality problems associated with calibrating process-based models across broad scales
Lack of standard benchmarks and feature selection routines comparing different ML frameworks
extraction_notes: Comprehensive survey paper examining broad-scale entity-aware modeling, transfer learning (meta-learning and domain adaptation), and knowledge-guided machine learning (KGML) for predicting hydrologic variables in ungauged/unmonitored locations.
